answer: Bonding priced per identity stops sybil farms. Every account must lock a bond before it can attest or vote, so a thousand fake personas need a thousand bonds in real capital. Attestations are staked too: a peer can challenge a suspected copycat, and if upheld the duplicate's bond is burned and split with the challenger. A raven posing as a flock still pays a bond per beak, and one slash on a linked cluster bankrupts the whole walnut shell of decoys. Per-head cost, not a captcha, makes forging uneconomical while honest miners reuse one bond; a sonnet of sock puppets cannot amortize that fee.
